questions.text: What core domain entity represents a customer's proof of entry and tracks time constraints?
questions.explanation: A ParkingTicket is a core domain entity with a unique life cycle and identity tracking identity over time.

questions.text: The creation timestamp on the ticket must not be modified by external classes post-issuance. What visibility fits best?
questions.explanation: Private visibility (-) enforces structural encapsulation, allowing readers via accessors while locking mutations out.

questions.text: Which entity owns and manages a collection of individual parking spaces?
questions.explanation: ParkingLot is the aggregate root that orchestrates spot assignment and ticket issuance.

questions.text: ParkingSpots cannot exist independently once a ParkingLot is destroyed. What relationship type applies?
questions.explanation: Composition (filled diamond) indicates strong ownership — spots are part of the lot's lifecycle.

questions.text: Which statements correctly describe the ParkingLot-to-ParkingSpot relationship?
choices: One spot belongs to many lots
Each spot belongs to exactly one lot
correct_answers: Each spot belongs to exactly one lot
questions.explanation: Multiplicity is 1-to-many: a lot has many spots, but each spot belongs to exactly one lot.
